arxiv-2003-11116.title: A characterization of high transitivity for groups acting on trees
arxiv-2003-11116.creator: Yves Stalder
arxiv-2003-11116.description: Abstract We establish a sharp sufficient condition for groups acting on trees to be highly transitive when the action on the tree is minimal of general type. This gives new examples of highly transitive groups, including icc non-solvable Baumslag-Solitar groups, thus answering a question of Hull and Osin.

arxiv-2010-13118.title: Monocular Depth Estimation via Listwise Ranking using the Plackett-Luce Model
arxiv-2010-13118.creator: Julian Lienen 1, Eyke Hüllermeier 2 Ralph Ewerth 3,4 Nils Nommensen 3,4 1 Paderborn University 2 University of Munich (LMU) 3 L3S Research Center, Leibniz University Hannover 4 TIB Hannover
arxiv-2010-13118.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Julian Lienen 1, Eyke Hüllermeier 2 Ralph Ewerth 3,4 Nils Nommensen 3,4 1 Paderborn University 2 University of Munich (LMU) 3 L3S Research Center, Leibniz University Hannover 4 TIB Hannover. In many real-world applications, the relative depth of objects in an image is crucial for scene understanding. Recent approaches mainly tackle the problem of depth prediction in monocular images by treating the problem as a regression task.

arxiv-2011-09109.title: On Simultaneous Long-Short Stock Trading Controllers with Cross-Coupling
arxiv-2011-09109.creator: Atul Deshpande, John A. Gubner, B. Ross Barmish
arxiv-2011-09109.description: Abstract The Simultaneous Long-Short (SLS) controller for trading a single stock is known to guarantee positive expected value of the resulting gain-loss function with respect to a large class of stock price dynamics. In the literature, this is known as the Robust Positive Expectation (RPE) property.

arxiv-2210-11727.title: Minimal Length, Nuclear Matter, and Neutron Stars Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2210-11727.creator: I. Prasetyo e1,addr2,addr3, I. H. Belfaqih e2,addr2,addr3, A. B. Wahidin e3,addr4,addr5, A. Suroso e4,addr6, A. Sulaksono e5,addr1
arxiv-2210-11727.description: Abstract In this paper, we employ one variant of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) model, i.e., the Kempf-Mangano-Mann (KMM) model, and discuss the impact of GUP on the EoS of nuclear and neutron star matter based on the Relativistic Mean Field (RMF) model.

arxiv-2303-12598.creator: D. Vohl ,, H. K. Vedantham, J. W. T. Hessels, C. G. Bassa, D. O. Cook, D. L. Kaplan, T. W. Shimwell, C. Zhang
arxiv-2303-12598.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by D. Vohl ,, H. K. Vedantham, J. W. T. Hessels, C. G. Bassa, D. O. Cook, D. L. Kaplan, T. W. Shimwell, C. Zhang. The vast majority of extragalactic compact continuum radio sources are associated with star formation or jets from (super)massive black holes and, as such, are more likely to be found in association with starburst galaxies or early-type galaxies.

arxiv-2306-08761.title: Rate of escape of the conditioned two-dimensional simple random walk
arxiv-2306-08761.creator: Orphée Collin, Serguei Popov
arxiv-2306-08761.description: Abstract We prove sharp asymptotic estimates for the rate of escape of the two-dimensional simple random walk conditioned to avoid a fixed finite set. We derive it from asymptotics available for the continuous analogue of this process [ 1 ] , with the help of a KMT-type coupling adapted to this setup.

arxiv-2403-09908.title: Electron screening and strength of long-range Coulomb interactions in phosphorene: From bulk to nanoribbon
arxiv-2403-09908.creator: Farshad Bagherpour, Saeed Mahdavifar, Elham Hosseini Lapasar, Hanif Hadipour
arxiv-2403-09908.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Farshad Bagherpour, Saeed Mahdavifar, Elham Hosseini Lapasar, Hanif Hadipour. Experimental observations of anisotropic tightly bound excitons in black phosphorene, and correlated phenomena such as room temperature magnetically active edges in phosphorene nanoribbons (PNRs), sparked discussions on the controversial screening of the Coulomb interaction in phosphorene-based materials. In this way, we investigate the first-principles electronic screening of the long-range Coulomb interaction in black phosphorene from bulk to nanoribbon by employing ab initio calculations in conjunction with the constrained random-phase approximation.

arxiv-2404-03732.title: SHROOM-INDElab at SemEval-2024 Task 6: Zero- and Few-Shot LLM-Based Classification for Hallucination Detection
arxiv-2404-03732.creator: Bradley P. Allen, Fina Polat, Paul Groth
arxiv-2404-03732.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bradley P. Allen, Fina Polat, Paul Groth. We describe the University of Amsterdam Intelligent Data Engineering Lab team’s entry for the SemEval-2024 Task 6 competition. The SHROOM-INDElab system builds on previous work on using prompt programming and in-context learning with large language models (LLMs) to build classifiers for hallucination detection, and extends that work through the incorporation of context-specific definition of task, role, and target concept, and automated generation of examples for use in a few-shot prompting approach.

arxiv-2405-01744.title: ALCM: Autonomous LLM-Augmented Causal Discovery Framework
arxiv-2405-01744.creator: Elahe Khatibi, Mahyar Abbasian, Zhongqi Yang, Iman Azimi, Amir M. Rahmani
arxiv-2405-01744.description: Abstract Abstract To perform effective causal inference in high-dimensional datasets, initiating the process with causal discovery is imperative, wherein a causal graph is generated based on observational data. However, obtaining a complete and accurate causal graph poses a formidable challenge, recognized as an NP-hard problem.

arxiv-2408-00311.title: Translating Imaging to Genomics: Leveraging Transformers for Predictive Modeling
arxiv-2408-00311.creator: Aiman Farooq, Deepak Mishra, Santanu Chaudhury
arxiv-2408-00311.description: Abstract In this study, we present a novel approach for predicting genomic information from medical imaging modalities using a transformer-based model. We aim to bridge the gap between imaging and genomics data by leveraging transformer networks, allowing for accurate genomic profile predictions from CT/MRI images.

arxiv-2408-13841.title: Bipolar blobs as evidence of hidden AGN activities in the low-mass galaxies Facilities: DESI, Sloan(MaNGA), Swift(XRT and UVOT) astropy ( Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , photutils ( Bradley et al. 2023 ) , reproject ( Robitaille et al. 2020 ) , Cloudy ( Chatzikos et al. 2023 ; Morisset 2013 ) , statmo
arxiv-2408-13841.creator: Yao Yao, Enci Wang, Zhicheng He, Zheyu Lin, Yu Rong, Hong-Xin Zhang, Xu Kong
arxiv-2408-13841.description: Abstract We report the evidence of a hidden black hole (BH) in a low-mass galaxy, MaNGA 9885-9102, and provide a new method to identify active BH in low mass galaxies. This galaxy is originally selected from the MaNGA survey with distinctive bipolar H α \alpha blobs at the minor axis.

arxiv-2411-03653.title: RoCK blocks of double covers of symmetric groups and generalized Schur algebras Thanks: The author was supported by the NSF grant DMS-2346684.
arxiv-2411-03653.creator: Alexander Kleshchev
arxiv-2411-03653.description: Abstract . We study blocks of the double covers of symmetric and alternating groups. The main result is a ‘local’ description, up to Morita equivalence, of arbitrary defect RoCK blocks of these groups in terms of generalized Schur superalgebras corresponding to an explicit Brauer tree superalgebra.

arxiv-2411-14983.title: Large sample scaling analysis of the Zig-Zag algorithm for Bayesian inference
arxiv-2411-14983.creator: Sanket Agrawal, Joris Bierkens, Gareth O. Roberts
arxiv-2411-14983.description: Abstract Piecewise deterministic Markov processes provide scalable methods for sampling from the posterior distributions in big data settings by admitting principled sub-sampling strategies that do not bias the output. An important example is the Zig-Zag process of [ Ann. Stats.

arxiv-2507-04883.title: Beyond Training-time Poisoning: Component-level and Post-training Backdoors in Deep Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2507-04883.creator: Sanyam Vyas 1,2 , Alberto Caron 2 , Chris Hicks 2 , Pete Burnap 1 , Vasilios Mavroudis 2 1 Cardiff University 2 The Alan Turing Institute vyass3@cardiff.ac.uk, acaron@turing.ac.uk, c.hicks@turing.ac.uk, burnapp@cardiff.ac.uk, vmavroudis@turing.ac.uk
arxiv-2507-04883.description: Abstract Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) systems are increasingly used in safety-critical applications, yet their security remains severely underexplored. This work investigates backdoor attacks, which implant hidden triggers that cause malicious actions only when specific inputs appear in the observation space. Existing DRL backdoor research focuses solely on training-time attacks requiring full adversarial access to the training pipeline.

pmc-10682755.title: Optimal decision-making in high-throughput virtual screening pipelines
pmc-10682755.creator: Hyun-Myung Woo, Xiaoning Qian, Li Tan, Shantenu Jha, Francis J Alexander, Edward R Dougherty, Byung-Jun Yoon
pmc-10682755.description: SummaryThe need for efficient computational screening of molecular candidates that possess desired properties frequently arises in various scientific and engineering problems, including drug discovery and materials design. However, the enormous search space containing the candidates and the substantial computational cost of high-fidelity property prediction models make screening practically challenging.

pmc-11487856.title: Protocol for a scoping review of older informal carers and digital health service use
pmc-11487856.creator: Emanuela Sala, Federica Cretazzo
pmc-11487856.description: IntroductionThe ageing population and increasing demands for healthcare pose challenges for national health services, which are increasingly looking to digital health services (DHS) as a potential solution. However, older informal carers, who provide unpaid care, often lack the digital skills necessary to access and use DHS, placing them at risk of social exclusion.

pmc-11523888.title: Losartan-based nanocomposite hydrogel overcomes chemo-immunotherapy resistance by remodeling tumor mechanical microenvironment
pmc-11523888.creator: Xiaodong Hou, Yuting Shen, Bin Huang, Qiuyan Li, Shaoyue Li, Tingting Jiang, Xuexia Shan, Weichen Xu, Shuo Liu, Shengbo Wu, De Zhao, Anqi Zhu, Liping Sun, Huixiong Xu, Wenwen Yue
pmc-11523888.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Preclinical studies demonstrating high cure rates with PD1/PD-L1 combinations have led to numerous clinical trials, but emerging results are disappointing. These combined immunotherapies are commonly employed for patients with refractory tumors following prior treatment with cytotoxic agents. Here, we uncovered that the post-chemotherapy tumor presents a unique mechanical microenvironment characterized by an altered extracellular matrix (ECM) elasticity and increased stiffness, which facilitate the development of aggressive tumor phenotypes and confer resistance to checkpoint blocking therapy.

pmc-12540646.title: A new proposal for electrode positioning in dogs from the perspective of electrovectorcardiography
pmc-12540646.creator: Marcelo de Sousa Londe, Nelson Samesima, Giovanni Naves Canta, Viviane Feliciana Xavier, Fabiana Silva Fadel Queiroz, Rodrigo Corrêa Fonseca Machado, Euler Fraga Silva, Horacio Gomes Pereira Filho, Bruna Affonso Madaloso, Caio de Assis Moura Tavares, Carlos Alberto Pastore
pmc-12540646.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Research on electrocardiology in dogs has primarily relied on methods developed for human cardiology, specifically in placing electrodes on the limbs and thorax. However, these methods do not consider the canine heart’s unique anatomical structure and electrophysiological characteristics. In this study, we propose a new arrangement of electrodes that aligns better with the anatomy of the canine heart by creating planes and axes that are more suitable for this species.

pmc-12707007.title: Social ecological model for developing health-promoting schools and improving healthy eating in female students: a mixed-method protocol study in Iran
pmc-12707007.creator: Farzaneh Pourjalil, Nahid Shahabi, Zahra Hosseini, Teamur Aghamolaei
pmc-12707007.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe concept of health-promoting schools, initiated by the World Health Organization, aims to move beyond individual behavior change and includes changes in the organizational structure, such as improvements in the physical and social environment of the school. By integrating health promotion into all aspects of life, health-promoting schools aim to equip students with the knowledge, skills, and supportive environment required to make healthy choices and develop lifelong healthy behaviors.

pmc-12733530.title: Evaluation of Factors Associated with Intracranial Hemorrhage in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department with Head Trauma: A Prospective Observational Study
pmc-12733530.creator: Kubra Parpucu Bagceci, Pakize Gozde Gok, Filiz Baloglu Kaya, Nurdan Acar, Engin Ozakin, Evvah Karakilic, Mustafa Emin Canakci, Katja E Wartenberg, Lori Shutter
pmc-12733530.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Head trauma is one of the most common causes of morbidity and mortality in emergency departments. It is essential to understand the factors leading to intracranial hemorrhage (IH) in order to improve outcomes and reduce healthcare costs. The aim of this study was to evaluate the factors associated with IH in patients presenting to the emergency department with head trauma.

pmc-13348616.title: Conditioned medium from the inflammatory microenvironment of human dental pulp stem cells regulated functional pulp regeneration
pmc-13348616.creator: Qian Zhang, Hengwei Zhang, Linting Wei, Bin Yang, Xiaofan Bai, Jianping Ruan, Ning Dong
pmc-13348616.description: ObjectiveThis study explored the effects of inflammatory microenvironment on stem cells from the apical papilla (SCAP) for cell homing strategy-based pulp regeneration.MethodsDental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) were treated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) for 48 h, creating a conditioned medium (LPS-CM). The influence of LPS-CM on SCAP proliferation, migration, odontogenic and neurogenic differentiation, pro-angiogenetic effects, cell apoptosis and senescence were assessed.

pmc-13371120.title: Decoupled accumulation of chlorophylls and total carotenoids between floral and vegetative organs in Dendrobium
pmc-13371120.creator: Feng-Ping Zhang, Le Yu, Qi-Yong Huang, Han-Run Li, Shi-Bao Zhang
pmc-13371120.description: Chlorophylls and carotenoids constitute the predominant plant pigments, playing pivotal roles in photosynthesis, pollinator attraction, and defense against biotic and abiotic stress. However, differences in pigment composition between floral and vegetative organs, along with their functional coordination, remain poorly understood.

pmc-13435972.title: Differences in patient-centered burdens and economic outcomes based on sociodemographic characteristics and social determinants of health: a scoping review
pmc-13435972.creator: Sophia D’Angelo, Sydney Kirsch, Ella Shenkar, Olga Khavjou, Kristen Giombi

pmc-13455527.title: The Role of a Biological Membrane in Healing Full‐Thickness Cutaneous Wounds in Rats
pmc-13455527.creator: Ali Ghazi Atiyah, Thamer Jaddoa Shihab, Ismael I Hasan, Lipi Buch
pmc-13455527.description: BackgroundFull‐thickness wounds pose significant healing challenges due to their reduced regenerative capacity and prolonged inflammation.ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the healing potential of decellularized amniotic membrane (AM) as a biological dressing for the treatment of full‐thickness cutaneous wounds.MethodsIn this study, 18 healthy rats were evenly distributed between the control and treatment groups.

pmc-13464453.title: Quizartinib Resistance Mutations and Treatment Outcomes in Relapsed or Refractory FLT3‐ITD–Positive AML
pmc-13464453.creator: Yuichiro Semba, Toshihiro Miyamoto, Senji Kasahara, Yoshikane Kikushige, Takahiro Maeda, Goichi Yoshimoto, Shuichi Ota, Akio Saito, Yuho Najima, Hiroki Hosoi, Daigo Niiya, Koji Kato, Koji Nagafuji, Takashi Akasaka, Tomohiko Kamimura, Atsushi Takita, Maiko Narahara, Tadashi Toki, Koichi Iwanaga, Koji
pmc-13464453.description: Quizartinib is a FMS‐like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) inhibitor indicated for FLT3 internal tandem duplication (FLT3‐ITD)–positive acute myeloid leukemia (AML). We aimed to evaluate quizartinib resistance mechanisms, in addition to efficacy and safety outcomes, in patients with relapsed or refractory FLT3‐ITD–positive AML. This multicenter, single‐arm study in Japan (jRCTs071200015) enrolled 18 patients between May 2020 and December 2022.
